newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-ELS FIRES 66 BUT TRAILS TO LOCAL MAN BRADLEY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS FIRES 66 BUT TRAILS TO LOCAL MAN BRADLEY.

text.p: Defending champion Ernie Els posted a typically aggressive 66 on the opening day of the 3.4 million rand (745,000 dollar) South African Open, but unheralded local man Wayne Bradley clinched the lead with a brilliant 65 at Glendower on Thursday.
Bradley, 31, outscored two of world golf's superstars in Els and Welshman Ian Woosnam while Americanised South African Fulton Allem and Denmark's Thomas Bjorn also returned 66s.
Bradley, with just two wins on junior tours in Africa, felt his round was unspectacular.

"I putted well but I didn't really have to make any long ones. I bought a new driver the day before the tournament and that went very straight all day. I just drove straight and putted straight," Bradley said.

Els's round began poorly when a wayward eight-iron cost him a shot at the first hole. An over-hit wedge cost him another shot at the 13th but his round caught fire with an eagle at the 15th and he posted six birdies as well.

"I'm only playing one tournament in South Africa this year because I want to sharpen my game in the States very early to get ready for the Masters which I think is the major best suited to my game. Being defending champion I'm delighted to have started like this. This tournament means a heck of lot to me," Els told reporters.

Allem, originally from Free State, is now an extremely rare visitor to the country of his birth. His round also took off with a birdie on the 17th, his eighth hole. Driving accuracy was the key to his success.

"I hit 16 greens in regulation and also regained my confidence on the greens. I'm thrilled with how the South African PGA has managed to get a bunch of major winners here for our Open and it feels great to be up there."
Woosnam's renaissance in form continued with both length and accuracy off the tee earning him birdies at all four of the par fives. Bjorn also put his success down the biggest club in his bag.
"This course really rewards good drivers. I drove very well and I'm not surprised to see both Ernie and Ian at the top of the leaderboard. They are both excellent drivers," he said.
